name: HOMOCYSTEINE
description: Homocysteine measures amino acid levels and evaluates cardiovascular risk, vitamin B12/B6/folate deficiency, and thrombophilia. This test assesses methionine metabolism and identifies individuals at risk for vascular disease.

testdetails.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: Homocysteine is a sulfur-containing amino acid produced during methionine metabolism. Normal range is 5-15 µmol/L. Elevated levels (hyperhomocysteinemia) are associated with increased cardiovascular disease risk, stroke, and venous thrombosis. Causes include vitamin B12, B6, or folate deficiency, renal failure, hypothyroidism, and genetic disorders (MTHFR mutations). Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides accurate measurement. Fasting samples preferred. Used in cardiovascular risk assessment, especially in young patients with thrombosis or premature atherosclerosis. Treatment involves B vitamin supplementation. Homocysteine promotes endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress, contributing to atherosclerosis. Monitoring parameter for vitamin supplementation efficacy.
